Katamari architecture describes a trend in LLM-driven development where software accumulates features and code without regard for structural composition. Much like the mechanics of the video game Katamari Damacy, LLM agents tend to append code to existing systems to satisfy immediate prompts rather than integrating new logic into a cohesive, designed structure.

This process intensifies the "Big Ball of Mud" effect by rapidly increasing codebase volume while decreasing developer visibility and cognitive engagement. To combat this, potential solutions include requiring the manual rewriting of LLM-generated code to ensure human maintainability and understanding.

entry.title: BGP Hijack Targets Softaculous and Virtualizor
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | blog.apnic.net | source | discussion | hacker news

In August 2026, a Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) hijack targeted Softaculous Ltd—the developer of Virtualizor—to distribute malicious software updates. Attackers announced a more specific 162.55.80.0/24 prefix within Hetzner Online's (AS24940) address space, using a forged AS path to maintain RPKI validity. This allowed the adversary to intercept certificate validation traffic, obtain valid TLS certificates, and deliver a compromised Virtualizor update to a subset of users.

The incident illustrates how widespread BGP hijacks can bypass Multi-Perspective Issuance Corroboration (MPIC) by providing a controlled quorum of validation viewpoints to Certificate Authorities. To mitigate such risks, experts suggest that networks use strict Route Origin Authorizations (ROAs) that match the `maxLength` attribute to the actual routed prefix, rather than allowing overly broad prefixes.

entry.title: Mike Pall Explains Why C Compilers Struggle with Interpreter Loops
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | web.archive.org | source | discussion

Mike Pall explains why C compilers struggle to optimize interpreter main loops, noting that they often fail to handle the complex control-flow graphs inherent in switch-based dispatch. Key issues include "diamond-shaped" control flow that disrupts register allocation, the inability to distinguish between fast and slow paths, and the failure of standard heuristics when managing hundreds of slow paths.

In contrast, Pall suggests that hand-written assembly can achieve significantly better performance through fixed register assignments, isolating slow paths to preserve instruction cache density, and pre-decoding operands. These strategies allow interpreters like LuaJIT to bypass the limitations of general-purpose compilers to achieve high execution efficiency.

Notion has implemented a system based on Conflict-free Replicated Data Types (CRDTs) to manage concurrent editing within its block-based document model. Moving away from a "last write wins" approach, the architecture uses a Replicated Growable Array (RGA) structure to ensure that simultaneous edits from multiple users are merged deterministically without losing data.

The implementation supports rich text formatting by applying the Peritext algorithm for annotations such as bolding and hyperlinking. To maintain consistency when users split or move text across different blocks, Notion utilizes a hierarchical system of text slices, text instances, and search labels, allowing the system to locate and apply updates to the correct target fragments even as the document structure changes.

Software sandboxing is structured through defined system call (syscall) policy groups that categorize operations such as basic I/O, filesystem access, and networking.
